- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) or mixed, model often underestimates or lags; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is trending up.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5-10 days; apply downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch the reversal; increase forecast slope or add early correction term.
- Mean reversion bias: if model consistently forecasts above 30-day moving average, reduce forecast; if below, increase — especially if sentiment is neutral or weak.
- Horizon-specific: 1-3 day forecasts are often too volatile; smooth with sentiment-weighted average of recent 5-7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” (neutral), model tends to drift toward historical mean; anchor forecast to recent 10-day average unless sentiment flips.
